input.question: How are Nucleated Red Blood Cells and Reticulocytes Related?
input.ground_truth: During erythropoiesis (the development of red blood cells) the ripening precursor cells and their nuclei gradually get smaller and smaller in a number of stages. This all happens mainly within the red bonemarrow in so called "erythroblastic islands", small groups of proliferating erythrocyte precursor cells in various stages of differentiation. The last stage of nucleated RBC's are called "orthochromatic erythroblasts" or "normoblasts". After this stage they lose their nucleus and become reticulocytes. Reticulocytes have no nucleus but contain a lot of loose RNA within their cytoplasm. When reticulocytes enter the bloodstream they gradually lose this RNA and ripen into erytrocytes within about 2 days. Under normal circumstances you wont find nucleated red precursor cells in the peripheral bloodstream.
